clue.text: Length of time Henry IV's without horse

parts.note: Hal is the familiar name for Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the Henry IV pieces sit around the horse

parts.note: IV is the Roman numeral four
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A remark that King Henry IV is missing his steed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not 'lacking'; Prince Hal of the Henry IV plays is the convention behind HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty minutes is a standard span of time, so the phrase names a length of time.

clue.text: English author announced American director

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the author's name is matched by its sound

parts.note: H. G. Wells was an English novelist

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reads out the name of a British writer, then a Hollywood film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist H. G. Wells and Orson Welles, director of Citizen Kane, share a pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the American film director behind Citizen Kane, so the surname fits the definition.

clue.text: Islander getting half-hearted boost on island? Not so

indicators.note: half-hearted removes half of the doubled middle pair from the word for a boost

parts.note: a fillip is a stimulus or boost
no is the reply that something is not so

explanation.surface: A question about whether an islander gets a lift from being on an island, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' takes one of the two central Ls out of FILLIP, leaving FILIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Philippines, an island nation, is an islander of that country.

clue.text: Take some port, if finished lunch

indicators.note: Take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a drop of port once the meal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the T ending 'port' and continues through 'if' into 'finished'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal, so it means lunch.

clue.text: After church primate left for another place of worship

indicators.note: After places the monkey word behind the church abbreviation in the build

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An ape leaves a church and heads off to worship somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, different from the church named earlier in the clue.

clue.text: Carbon material, chalk or wax used by artist

definitions.text: chalk or wax used by artist

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rayon is a synthetic fabric or material

explanation.surface: A list of drawing media an artist might use, from carbon to chalk to wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing stick made of coloured wax or chalk is what an artist uses for colouring.

clue.text: Stays very short time in academic stream?

indicators.note: in puts the time abbreviation inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford, a university city
short says to abbreviate time to its letter T

explanation.surface: Someone spends brief periods by a university river.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISIS is the Thames at Oxford, hence 'academic stream'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay with someone for a while is to pay them visits, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Your statement of misfortune gets a raise in pay

indicators.note: in a down answer a raise lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of grief or misfortune

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark from you leads to a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a raise' turns the whole run YR ALAS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed regular pay for a job, so pay is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Personifying South American people new in classification

parts.note: the Inca were a people of the Andes in South America

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for new inside the word for classification

parts.note: a rating is a classification or grade

explanation.surface: A description of how a South American people is newly categorised.
explanation.definitionFit: To incarnate something is to embody it in a person, so incarnating means personifying.

clue.text: Loud blast that proved fatal for Claudius

definitions.meaning: a loud scolding or telling-off delivered at length
in Hamlet, Claudius murdered the old king by pouring poison into his ear, so an ear filled with poison was his fatal method

explanation.surface: A noisy explosion that killed the Roman emperor or the Danish king.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as 'ear full': in Hamlet the poison poured in the sleeping king's ear was Claudius's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long angry telling-off, a loud blast of criticism, and literally an ear full of something.

clue.text: Secure collection of data that you may need at your fingertips

definitions.text: that you may need at your fingertips

parts.note: to nail is to fasten or secure
a file is a stored collection of data

explanation.surface: Advice to protect a data file you need close to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at your fingertips' usually means readily available; here it is literal, the tool used on fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: A small abrasive tool for shaping nails is used literally at the fingertips.

clue.text: Engine round the bend

definitions.meaning: short for locomotive, a railway engine
crazy, a sense taken from Spanish

explanation.definitionFit: Loco is both an abbreviation for a railway locomotive and slang for crazy.

clue.text: Transformed into art, say, like a statue

indicators.note: Transformed says the letters of the following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something turned into a work of art, standing as still as a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges the ten letters of INTO ART SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue does not move, so being motionless is being like a statue.

clue.text: Problems in other across answers needing setter's attention

definitions.text: Problems in other across answers needing setter's attention

parts.words: Problems in other across answers needing setter's attention
parts.note: a setter here is one who sets fractures, as a bonesetter does; each pair of neighbouring across answers hides a skeletal part split across the gap

explanation.walkthrough: The skeletal parts are split across neighbouring across answers: PELVIS in CHAPEL VISITS, ULNA in EARFUL NAILFILE, COSTA in LOCO STATIONARY, TALUS in ORNAMENTAL USED, ANVIL in BERMUDAN VILEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractures are injuries that a bonesetter attends to, and the theme entries contain fractured skeletal parts.

clue.text: Reportedly short of manual work

indicators.note: Reportedly says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: being short of something is needing it

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that there is not enough work done by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the two words are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Working dough with the hands is a classic example of manual labour.

clue.text: English characteristic — fair treatment for all

parts.note: a quality is a characteristic or attribute

explanation.surface: A claim that fairness to everyone is a typically English trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle that everyone has the same rights and status is fair treatment for all.

clue.text: Places for putting a group of politicians

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, the smooth areas where the ball is putted towards the hole
members of an environmentalist party, known collectively by its colour

explanation.definitionFit: Golf greens are where players putt, and the Greens are an environmentalist political party.

clue.text: Tricky question presenting no difficulty in test paper, ultimately

indicators.note: in puts the word for no difficulty between the two final letters
ultimately points to the last letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: ease is the absence of difficulty

explanation.surface: An exam paper sets a hard question but the candidate finds it simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser, short for brainteaser, is a puzzling or tricky question.

clue.text: In exam identify sacred books with embellishment

indicators.note: In puts the naming word and the scripture abbreviation inside the word for the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
to name is to identify
NT is the New Testament, a set of sacred books

explanation.surface: During an exam a candidate names scriptures and dresses up the answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental describes something decorative, serving as embellishment.

clue.text: Awful dream I think a lot of

indicators.note: Awful suggests something badly messed up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to dwelling on a dreadful dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high esteem is to think a lot of them.

clue.text: Raised voice, finally, with verse in song

indicators.note: in puts the final letter and the verse abbreviation inside the song word

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of voice

explanation.surface: A singer lifts their voice at the end of a verse in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIED is a German art song, a classical crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a tax is to raise it, so levied means raised.

clue.text: Exploited conclusions reached by you, as we did

indicators.note: conclusions points to the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone feels taken advantage of, having come to the same conclusions as us.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to use them, so exploited and used are synonyms.

clue.text: Islander dividing a number that's odd by 500

indicators.note: dividing says the Roman figure splits the rearranged letters
that's odd tells us the letters of the phrase before are scrambled

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An island resident does some arithmetic, dividing an odd number by 500.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's odd' rearranges A NUMBER into BERMUAN; 'dividing' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Bermuda, an Atlantic island territory, is an islander.

clue.text: Extremely nasty half-dozen in case

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six, half a dozen
lest means in case or for fear that

explanation.surface: Six of something are terribly unpleasant, just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of vile means most nasty, so extremely nasty fits.

clue.text: After call for quiet, row diminished

indicators.note: After places the row word behind the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the noise made to ask for quiet
a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Once someone asked for silence, the argument died down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line, RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that shrank grew smaller, so it diminished.

clue.text: Landlord's strict verbal interpretation

definitions.meaning: one who lets property to tenants
as in the ... of the law, a reading that sticks to the exact words

explanation.definitionFit: A person who lets property is a letter, and the letter of the law is its strict literal meaning.
